description: The image displays two side-by-side bar charts, each illustrating the relationship between a measure of ambiguity and Fleiss Kappa, a statistical measure of inter-rater reliability. The left chart, titled "Ambiguity Std," plots Fleiss Kappa on the vertical axis (ranging from 0.0 to 0.8) against four distinct values of "Ambiguity Std" on the horizontal axis: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. The bars, colored in a dark teal, show a general decreasing trend in Fleiss Kappa as ambiguity standard deviation increases, with values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 respectively. The right chart, titled "Max Ambiguity," plots Fleiss Kappa on the vertical axis (ranging from 0.0 to 0.8) against three values of "Max Ambiguity" on the horizontal axis: 1, 2, and 3. The bars, also in dark teal, show a decreasing trend in Fleiss Kappa as maximum ambiguity increases, with values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23 respectively. Both charts use a consistent scale for the vertical axis and clearly label each bar with its corresponding numerical value.
